content.user_title: Build Azure Hosted Agents in Python
content.value_statement: Azure hosted agent setup can be unclear when container images, protocols, and credentials must align. This skill gives Python patterns for Azure AI Projects hosted agents.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to create an AIProjectClient with DefaultAzureCredential.
Demonstrates ImageBasedHostedAgentDefinition for container-based hosted agents.
Explains protocol version records for AgentProtocol.RESPONSES.
Covers container image, CPU, memory, tools, and environment variable settings.
Includes patterns for listing and deleting agent versions.
Provides synchronous and asynchronous Python examples.
limitations: It does not provision Azure resources or container registries.
It does not verify SDK behavior against a live Azure tenant.
It assumes the Azure AI Projects SDK supports hosted agents.
It provides examples, not a complete production deployment pipeline.

use_cases.title: Create a first hosted agent
use_cases.description: Use the basic client and hosted agent example to connect a Python container image to Azure AI Foundry.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent configuration
use_cases.description: Review required parameters, protocol versions, tools, and resource settings before publishing container-based agents.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot deployment setup
use_cases.description: Use the common error table and prerequisites to check registry access, capability hosts, and protocol settings.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic hosted agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup with one container image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a Python Azure AI hosted agent using ImageBasedHostedAgentDefinition, DefaultAzureCredential, and one container image.

prompt_templates.title: Add tools and environment variables
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure tools, CPU, memory, and environment variables for an Azure AI hosted agent in Python.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a production configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup with stable images and resource choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Azure AI hosted agent settings and suggest safer image tags, resource values, and required Azure prerequisites.

prompt_templates.title: Design an async deployment flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation using asynchronous SDK clients.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an asynchronous Python workflow for creating an Azure AI hosted agent and explain each required SDK object.

output_examples.input: I need a hosted agent that runs a custom data processor image.
output: A concise setup plan with required Azure prerequisites.
A Python client creation pattern using DefaultAzureCredential.
A hosted agent definition covering image, protocol, CPU, memory, and tools.

output_examples.input: My hosted agent cannot pull the container image.
output: A troubleshooting checklist for ACR image path, image tag, and AcrPull permissions.
A reminder to verify the project managed identity and capability host settings.

output_examples.input: I want to move from a synchronous example to async Python.
output: An async workflow outline using the asynchronous credential and project client.
Guidance on where to await hosted agent creation and how to return the created version.

best_practices: Use specific container image tags for production hosted agents.
Store configuration in environment variables or Azure Key Vault.
Delete unused agent versions after testing to reduce resource usage.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode secrets in hosted agent definitions.
Do not rely on latest image tags for production releases.
Do not skip ACR pull permissions or capability host checks.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you build Python hosted agents that run container images in Azure AI Foundry.

faq.question: Which SDK does it use?
faq.answer: It uses the Azure AI Projects SDK with ImageBasedHostedAgentDefinition and related model classes.

faq.question: Does it create Azure infrastructure for me?
faq.answer: No. It explains prerequisites and code patterns, but it does not provision Azure resources.

faq.question: Can I configure tools for the hosted agent?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show code interpreter, file search, and MCP tool configuration patterns.

faq.question: Does it support asynchronous Python?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an async pattern using asynchronous Azure credential and project client classes.

faq.question: Is this useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives structured prompts and examples that these assistants can apply when building Azure hosted agents.
